contents.content: Write a dialogue between two friends making dinner.
Instructions: Complete the following steps. Fill in the Self-Assessment.
Exchange advice and suggestions in communicative situations.
Requesting and Offering Help by E-mail

When you ask someone for help or advice, it is important to be very polite.

Here are some common sentences and expressions that are considered polite.

The Future with Will, Going to, the Present Simple
You can use three different tenses to talk about the future.
When you talk about things that are not decided or when you make a decision at the moment of speaking for the future, you use the modal will.
When you ask about intentions, you use be going to.
When you talk about things that are scheduled, like programs, classes, buses or trains, you use the Present Simple tense.

Example: Come over here and cut up these yellow peppers.
These are words you use when you are preparing a meal with a friend.
to take the seeds out of a vegetable or fruit
Example: Can you seed the yellow peppers for me, please?
Example: Do whichever you think is easiest for you.
to roll into a tight space
Example: You should curl back your fingers so you don't cut them.
to set your radio or TV to catch a channel
Example: Tune into radio station KZ 2740 for great music all day long!
Write a dialogue between two people who are making a meal together.
One person will ask for advice and the other person will give advice about cooking.
Use who, that or which to express a complex idea.
I write a dialogue about making a meal.
I ask for advice and offer help.
